prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / mobile composition redesign.
INPUT 1 is the existing rocky game background. INPUT 2 is the rocky battle board, a PALETTE reference for the ground only. Keep the same overhead ground, thick near-black plum outlines, simple 2–3 tone cartoon cel shading and gray/taupe stone with muted lavender shadows. Do not include the board or any grid.
REDRAW THE COMPOSITION for a TALL NARROW 9:20 portrait canvas, 1080 x 2400 pixels. This is a full-screen mobile battle backdrop with game UI drawn over it. Do not squeeze or stretch the old 3:4 layout. Recompose naturally for the new tall aspect ratio.
VERY IMPORTANT PLACEMENT: The UPPER 0–52% of the image is quiet pale rocky ground with only small subtle unoutlined flecks; a battle board will hide most of that area. The MAIN DECORATIVE DETAIL belongs in the LOWER-MIDDLE exposed band, between 57% and 73% of canvas height (approximately y=1370–1750). Keep every essential accent wholly within the MIDDLE THIRD of the WIDTH (approximately x=360–720), so it remains visible when sides are cropped. Avoid putting important features only at far edges or at the very bottom, which the creature tray covers.
Within that lower-middle central band arrange a SMALL, NATURAL ASYMMETRICAL GROUP of DIFFERENT low ground features, not a line or repeating pebble pairs: one small broad flat angular stone with a tiny muted olive moss corner, centered near (475,1460), about 170 pixels wide; one irregular shallow blue-gray puddle, centered near (625,1640), about 150 pixels wide and 65 pixels tall, with one simple pale reflection; one short weathered brown root curving near (420,1660), about 95 pixels long, with at most one branch. Include only two or three tiny loose chips at varied offsets. Give these accents confident rounded dark-plum outlines around 8–11 pixels thick at output size and broad simple flat colors. They should look like the same artist's game icons. Keep them understated and leave substantial clear floor between shapes. The stone, puddle and root must have distinct silhouettes and unequal spacing; no repeated motif, rows, symmetry or regular border rhythm. No large rocks or raised features in the middle.
A FEW optional secondary details may sit closer to the side edges: a small cropped flat ledge around left edge at 40% height and a modest rounded stone nearer right edge at 67%, with very little height or shadow. These are expendable if cropped; the important little lower-middle group must be fully inside the central third. Do not repeat large boulders all down the sides. Lower 78–100% mostly returns to simple low-contrast ground because the tray covers it.
Match the LIGHT ground colors of input 2 so the separate board reads as marked ground within this surface. Keep the existing small-scale stone patch texture, but subdued, clean and low contrast. No dense grit or speckle noise. STRICT TOP-DOWN bird's-eye ground view; no horizon, ceiling, cave walls, tall cliffs, landscape perspective, spotlight or dramatic shadows. No characters, text, symbols, labels, grid, purple divider, board-shaped panel or frame. Opaque full bleed. Output only one finished 1080 x 2400 mobile background.
refinement_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Keep this exact tall 9:20 overhead rocky game background and all its style and floor colors. Output 1080 x 2400 pixels. Correct ONLY the lower-middle decorative group for a narrow mobile safe area.
The main mossy stone, blue-gray puddle, and brown root must each fit COMPLETELY inside the central third of the canvas width, INCLUDING their outlines: between 34% and 66% of the width. The current puddle reaches too far right and the root too far left. Shrink each of these three main shapes to about 75–80% of its current width and height. Move the puddle slightly LEFT. Move the root slightly RIGHT. Keep the stone near 44% of canvas width and 61% of its height; puddle near 57% width and 67% height; root near 43% width and 70% height. The group stays asymmetrical, with loose space between its three different silhouettes. Neither the stone, root, puddle nor their thick outline may extend outside 34–66% of canvas width. All three features remain fully within 57–74% of total height, above where the bottom tray begins. This is the main visible detail in the strip under the board on tall phones.
Keep the little scattered companion chips sparse. Keep the secondary far-edge stone fragments where they are; they are not key features. Keep the entire upper 52% quiet and free of new detail, and keep the very bottom quiet. Preserve strong deep-plum rounded outlines and broad 2–3 tone cel shading; no thin lines, realistic textures or extra detail. The puddle outline must be the same deep plum color as the stone and root outline, with a restrained blue-gray fill. Preserve the pale warm-gray/taupe ground and strict top-down perspective. No board, grid, divider, text, labels, walls, horizon, shadows around a panel or creatures.
safe_area_refinement_prompt: Precise localized image edit. Keep this entire 1080 x 2400, 9:20 rocky background unchanged, including every stone, root, moss patch, ground mark and outline. Move ONLY the blue-gray puddle in the lower middle horizontally LEFT by exactly 4 percent of the full canvas width (about 43 pixels on a 1080-pixel-wide canvas). Preserve its exact size, shape, shading, thick dark-plum outline and vertical position. Erase its old placement cleanly back to the same ground texture. Its new complete horizontal span should be approximately 46%–65% of canvas width, so its entire outline fits inside the central third. Do not move or resize any of the surrounding stones, the brown root, companion chips, or far-edge rocks. Do not change the composition, camera, colors, resolution, lighting or detail density. Do not add anything. Output only the finished image with that single small puddle translation.
